Al Francis Librero has advised two theses in this repository, both of which were completed in 2012. Their supervision patterns show a focus on the intersection of arts, technology, and digital learning environments. The first thesis supervised was "Biomodd Do-It-Yourself Manual" by Blaise Cedrick N. Gomez, which addressed environment and sustainability through the lens of collaborative art and electronic elements. The second thesis supervised was "Technical Challenges with E-Learning Tools: A Bachelor of Arts in Multimedia Studies Case Study" by Joanna Camila T. Leongson, which focused on online and distance learning, arts and creative practice, and educational technology. Based on these two supervised works, their research interests appear to involve the practical application of technology within creative and educational contexts.

Beyond thesis supervision, Al Francis Librero has three articles in this repository. These publications cover a range of sub-topics including arts and creative practice, online and distance learning, environment and sustainability, educational technology, information systems, and open educational resources. Their work includes an article from 2011 titled "Biomodd: A Case Study In Combining Online Learning With On-Site New Media Art Practice," which examines a blended learning approach for integrating online learning with on-site new media art practice. Another article from 2014, "Biomodd: Exploring Relationships Between Biological, Electronic, And Social Systems Through New Media Art," co-authored with Diego S. Maranan, investigates the intersection of art, science, and technology. A third article, "Student Co-Creation in an Online University: successes, failures, and how to move forward," published in 2019, focuses on open educational resources, arts and creative practice, and online and distance learning.

The evidence regarding their current research activity is limited to items in this repository, with the latest item dated 2026, though they had no advisees recorded for that year. Their primary strengths, as indicated by their published work and supervised theses, lie in the areas of arts and creative practice and online and distance learning. They demonstrate an interest in how new media art, electronic systems, and social systems interact, as well as the technical and pedagogical challenges associated with e-learning and multimedia studies. While their supervision history in this repository is limited to the year 2012, their published articles suggest a sustained interest in the relationship between digital learning environments and creative practice.

Based on the items in this repository, their work frequently addresses the complexities of new media art and how it interacts with biological, electronic, and social systems. They have contributed to discussions regarding student co-creation within online university environments and the use of open educational resources. Their research also touches upon technical challenges encountered with e-learning tools and the integration of online learning with on-site new media art practice. The sub-topics identified across their items include arts and creative practice, which appears four times, online and distance learning, which appears three times, environment and sustainability, educational technology, information systems, and open educational resources. Through their articles, they have explored how blended learning approaches can support community building and how new media art can serve as a case study for combining online and on-site practices.

In terms of thesis supervision, Al Francis Librero has advised two theses in this repository, both of which were completed in 2012. Their supervision patterns show an interest in topics such as environment and sustainability, online and distance learning, arts and creative practice, and educational technology. The first thesis they advised, titled "Biomodd Do-It-Yourself Manual" in 2012, focused on environment and sustainability and addressed the need for instructional resources for participants in the Biomodd collaborative art project. The second thesis, "Technical Challenges with E-Learning Tolls: A Bachelor of Arts in Multimedia Studies Case Study" (2012), focused on online and distance learning, arts and creative practice, and educational technology, specifically investigating the role and difficulties of technology in distance education at the University of the Philippines Open University. While they have published three articles in this repository, their most recent activity in the repository is dated 2026, though they have no advisee listed for that year. Their latest recorded advisee year is 2012. The evidence regarding their current supervision capacity is limited to these two historical instances. Their research interests appear to bridge the gap between technical systems and creative expression, particularly within the context of distance education and collaborative art projects. They have examined how electronic elements and ecological life can be explored through new media art, and how technical challenges impact students in multimedia studies. Their work suggests a strength in examining the practical applications of technology within artistic and educational frameworks.
